register.title: Evan Daniel's n303 dilation certificate at f06521f, issue728
register.headline: Daniel's new n303 arrangement, found from Ostashev's packing, certified exactly
register.source_checks: The author reports that his two exact rational checkers, verify_cert.py (separating axes) and verify_cert2.py (polygon intersection), accept the certificate, with least pair separation 1.2e-12. The source states the certificate is a dilation of a binary64 packing (search/packer/dilate_cert.py): centres and box scaled by 1 + 10^-12, coordinates rounded to rationals and each angle to a rational half-angle tangent, so every square is exactly unit; it certifies the upper bound only. The source leaves local optimality unresolved: its exact solver finds the packing not first-order jammed, and its corner-corner MILP predicts a further first-order descent of about 4.8e-7 that its descent step did not realise. It calls the packing new, not a refinement of Ostashev's #562 packing (matching distance 0.266, 91 tilted squares against 92). Those are the source's numerical statements. No source program ran here.
register.credit: Credit Evan Daniel (https://github.com/evand/square-packing), whose basin explorer started from Daniil Ostashev's #562 packing and whose near-record sweeps, crossovers and a final band flip, one tilted band reflected along its wall, reached this packing, as the issue says. The search, the checks and the request were done with Claude (Claude Code) under Evan Daniel's direction.
register.next_rung: Independently review the retained replay, then adopt at 303.
